entries.name: Pallof Press
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the band anchored behind the athlete's back. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 60 degrees so the anchor is seen out to the athlete's side: standing side-on to an anchored band held at the centre of the chest; the hands press straight out to long arms, hold, and return, and nothing else moves. The band stretches a little as the hands go out.
entries.summary: Standing side-on to an anchored band held at the chest, press to long arms with the shoulders and hips square, pause, then return to the chest.

frames.caption: Stand side-on to an anchored band and hold it at the centre of the chest in a stable stance.
Press to long arms while the shoulders and hips stay square.
Keep the shoulders and hips square.

entries.name: Pallof Press With Rotation
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the pulley behind the athlete's back. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 60 degrees so the pulley is seen out to the athlete's side: standing side-on to a shoulder-height pulley with the handle at the chest; press straight out, then the shoulders turn a quarter turn away from the pulley with the arms straight and the hips and legs still, a pause, a slower return to face forward, and the handle comes back to the chest. The cable only lengthens through the press and the turn. One side is shown; the last caption carries the change of sides.
entries.summary: Standing side-on to a shoulder-height pulley, press the handle straight out, turn the torso a quarter turn away with the arms straight and the hips still, then return slowly and bring the handle back to the chest.

frames.caption: Set the pulley at shoulder height, stand side-on to it with the feet hip-width apart and hold the handle in both hands at the chest.
Keeping the hips still and the arms straight, turn the torso away from the pulley through a quarter turn.
Arms straight, turn from the ribs.
Bring the handle back to the chest, then face the other way after the set.
